title: A Radio Call About a Stranger on a Night Train
script: Radio Host: [cheerfully] Good evening, listeners! Tonight we want stories about kindness from strangers while traveling. Our first caller is on the line. Hello!
Caller: [warmly] Hello! I have a story from a night train I took two winters ago, if that counts.
Radio Host: [encouraging] Perfect, exactly what we're looking for tonight. Please, go ahead.
Caller: [reflective] I was traveling alone, heading home after a difficult week, and I hadn't slept properly in days.
Radio Host: [gently] What happened once you boarded the train that night?
Caller: [thoughtful] An older woman sat across from me, and although I usually avoid conversations with strangers, she started talking anyway.
Radio Host: [curious] Did that bother you, given how tired you already were?
Caller: [honestly] At first, yes, a little. But something about her voice was calm, so I found myself answering her questions.
Radio Host: [interested] What did you two talk about during the journey?
Caller: [warmly] Everything, actually. My job, my family, even why my eyes looked so tired that particular evening.
Radio Host: [curious] Did you tell her what was really bothering you?
Caller: [emotional] Eventually, yes. I mentioned I had lost my job that week, something I hadn't told anyone else yet.
Radio Host: [sympathetically] That's a heavy thing to carry alone. How did she respond?
Caller: [with feeling] She didn't offer advice immediately. She just listened, which honestly was exactly what I needed at that moment.
Radio Host: [curious] Did she say anything that stayed with you afterward?
Caller: [softly] She said, every closed door on a train eventually opens onto a different platform, so don't panic about this one yet.
Radio Host: [warmly] That's a beautiful way to put it. Did you ever see her again after that train ride?
Caller: [reflective] No, she left at an earlier station than mine, and we never exchanged information, not even names.
Radio Host: [curious] Do you think about her often, even now, years later?
Caller: [warmly] Constantly, actually. Especially whenever I face something uncertain, I remember her calm voice on that quiet night train.
